paper_id: Xiang et al. - 2015 - Calibrate without Calibrating An Iterative Approach in Participatory Sensing Network
title: Calibrate without Calibrating: An Iterative Approach in Participatory Sensing Network
motivation: Participatory sensing participants are uncooperative and uncontrollable; existing calibration methods require collaboration or explicit calibration process
problem_framing: Joint estimation of sensor noise, source presences, and source parameters as MLE problem with three tightly coupled unknowns
key_insight: Sensing diversity across multiple sources enables implicit calibration: a participant sensing multiple pollution sources provides enough structure to estimate sensor noise without explicit calibration
method_signature: Two-level EM-like iterative algorithm (ACTION): outer loop estimates source presences, inner loop alternates between sensor noise and source parameter estimation
evaluation_criteria: Estimation accuracy of sensor bias and noise deviation compared with ML-H1, ML-H0, and EM-TS baseline methods
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Initial values have slight influence on calibration accuracy due to convergence; sampling frequency is tradeoff between calibration accuracy and energy cost
evidence_for_taste: calibrate sensors without explicit or cooperative calibrating process
expected likelihood increases step by step
thinking_moves: 把三个相互耦合的未知量拆解成两层迭代结构，化整为零
利用参与者自然漫游产生的 sensing diversity 作为隐式约束条件
将不可控的校准问题重新 frame 成最大似然估计问题
先证 expected likelihood 是 likelihood 的下界，再证明最优解等价性
